headline: Rebound day: KSE-100 closed UP 1,021.39pts (+0.61%) at 169,043.19 on Thu Sep 17, clawing back most of Wednesday's 1,370pt selloff. Banks, cement, E&P, refineries, OMCs and autos led gains after US President Trump said the Iran war could be nearing an end and oil prices eased as Saudi Arabia rerouted crude via Oman while its East-West pipeline stays shut. Separately the Fed hiked its policy rate 25bps to 3.75-4% (first US hike since 2023) — a global tightening surprise that didn't dent PSX sentiment today given the local risk-on catalysts. Drawdown from the Jan 23 ATH (189,556) narrowed to ~10.8% (still past the 10% dry-powder trigger, still short of the 15% heavier-shift line). Portfolio ~Rs 10.08M, P/L ~-Rs 178,400 (~-1.74% on cost) — better than yesterday's ~-2.23%. No holding moved >5% (GHGL +4.8% was the largest single-day move, no company-specific news found behind it). AVN's EXIT call and the AICF/MICF dry-powder redeployment both remain unexecuted — index.html holdings (24,500 AVN shares, same AICF/MICF units) are unchanged from yesterday.
market: KSE-100: Thursday Sep 17 closed at 169,043.19, UP 1,021.39pts (+0.61%) — intraday range 168,222.91 to 169,576.52, volume 73.87M shares / Rs6.96bn traded value. Index-heavy names including Lucky Cement, MCB, Meezan Bank, National Bank, UBL, Mari, OGDC, PPL, POL and Attock Refinery traded green. The rally followed Trump's comment that the Iran war could be nearing an end, plus oil prices easing as reports surfaced of Saudi Arabia routing additional crude cargoes via Oman while its East-West Pipeline (shut since Sep 11, blamed on a pro-Iran Iraqi militia) undergoes repair — Brent ~$106.3/bbl, WTI ~$102.2/bbl, both off the ~$107.8/$104.6 highs of the past few days. Houthi militants separately struck Khamis Mushait, Abha and Taif in Saudi Arabia this week, and Pakistan's Mecca Joint Defence Agreement (Turkiye-Saudi-Pakistan) remains formally in place, but Pakistan has not moved beyond rhetoric — no new direct-Pakistan escalation and today's market action was clearly risk-on despite the ongoing regional friction. US Fed: raised its benchmark rate 25bps to 3.75-4% (unanimous), the first US hike since 2023 — a genuine surprise versus the market's 'hold' expectation, with no further hikes pencilled in for 2026 and one cut each indicated for 2028/2029; PSX did not react negatively to this today, but a firmer-for-longer Fed is worth watching as a drag on EM flows and PKR stability over time. SBP kept its policy rate unchanged at 11.5% on Sep 14 (second consecutive pause), consistent with IMF-program alignment. PKR: stable, USD/PKR ~277.9/278.45, no material move this week. AVN: no new company news since the Sep 2 H1 FY26 loss filing; EXIT call remains unexecuted across many consecutive reviews. EFERT: no new Q3 results or dividend news since the already-covered Sep 3 payment (Aug 10 ex-date); urea-glut WATCH stance unchanged. DRAP pharma pricing: still unresolved — the government (via Economic Affairs Minister Ahad Cheema) has directed DRAP to urgently review its pricing formula and the Hardship Policy, while industry associations continue to formally oppose changes, warning of supply disruption; no enactment yet, GLAXO/SEARL WATCH stance unchanged. These are accumulation guides, not precise buy/sell signals — verify with your broker.
